sentences.text: Reason:

The question that arose for consideration before the High Court was whether the subject acquisition, which commenced way back on 10.05.1989 (Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894) followed by notification dated 09.05.1990 (Section 6 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894), is said to have lapsed in view of Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (in short, the 2013 Act).

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 4. It is pertinent to note that in view of the authoritative pronouncement by Constitution Bench of this Court in Indore Development Authority vs. Manohar Lal and others, (2020) 8 SCC 129, it was sufficient for the acquiring authority to prove that; (i) either the possession of the acquired land had been taken by following the prescribed procedure; or (ii) the substantial part of the compensation determined by the Land Acquisition Collector had been deposited.

entities.text: Indore Development Authority vs. Manohar Lal and others, (2020) 8 SCC 129
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. In the instant case, the respondent-State, in its counter- affidavit, categorically took a stand that the possession of the acquired land had been taken vide Rapat Roznamcha No.437 dated 07.05.1992 and Mutation No.18066 dated 15.10.2002 was duly sanctioned in favour of the beneficiary department.

It was further categorically averred that the entire amount of compensation was tendered and out of the total awarded amount of Rs.11,41,92,576/-, a sum of Rs.8,31,04,049/- had been disbursed and the rest of the amount was lying deposited in the land acquisition account.

It was further categorically averred that the petitioner no.2 (Munish Kumar) has lifted the amount of compensation for his share in Khasra No.675/2, 676 min., which is disputed by the petitioners, and rest of the amount was lying deposited with the LAC account.

6. In view of the above-stated categorical factual stand having been taken before the High Court,
which went substantially unrebutted, we are satisfied that the High Court has correctly turned down the plea of acquisition having lapsed under Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act.

7. In fact, it appears from the judgment of the High Court that the petitioners were primarily harping upon a plea for the release of the land on the ground that its industrial unit was functional at the site.
Such a plea was partly allowed to the extent that the land was being utilised for industrial purposes.

It is only the remaining unutilised land, which has been acquired for the public purpose,
that the claim under Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act has been rejected.

8. In all fairness, learned senior counsel for the petitioners relies upon a decision of this Court in State of Haryana & Ors. vs. Aalamgir & Ors. (C.A. No.4052/2025 & connected appeals), whereby a batch of appeals arising out of the same acquisition have been remanded to the High Court for reconsideration of the plea of Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act.

entities.text: State of Haryana & Ors. vs. Aalamgir & Ors. (C.A. No.4052/2025 & connected appeals)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A perusal of that judgment would reveal that the High Court has been asked to call for the record and see whether any panchnama regarding the taking of possession was prepared, or is there any other proof regarding the taking of possession of the land.

Such an issue does not arise in the instant case, where, as noticed earlier, relevant documents re: taking possession were prepared, and mutation was duly sanctioned in favour of the beneficiary department.

sentences.text:
Consequently, we see no valid ground to entertain the special leave petitions, which are,
accordingly, dismissed.

10. However, having taken notice of the fact that a batch of matters has been remanded to the High Court only to find out a small factual issue, we request the High Court to list the remanded matters without any delay and make an endeavour to decide the same by the end of February 2026.

We are prompted to make such a request, keeping in mind that the acquisition took place way back in the year 1989-1990, and there are several rounds of litigation due to which the beneficiary department has not been able to utilise the land for the public purpose for which it was acquired.
11. It is clarified that this order, however, shall not preclude the petitioners from seeking the release of the unpaid compensation and/or seeking further enhancement in accordance with the law.
12. All pending applications, if any, also stand disposed of.

(ARJUN BISHT) (PREETHI T.C.)
ASTT.
